threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still go to the green grocer expecting normal prices instead of debating whether to splurge on heirloom tomatoes.
Caught a bloke sleeping with a full kebab in his hand on the 59 last night. When the bus lurched, he didn't even flinch. Proper legend.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw an old man feeding pigeons while chatting about poetry with a street artist near the canal. It felt like magic in the chaos.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a Späti that doubles as an art gallery—local artists showcase their work alongside your midnight beer run.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they're locals when they know not to even glance at the BART app during rush hour—it’ll just ruin your day.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: One time, a musician jumped on the 47, played a haunting tune, and by the next stop, everyone was smiling despite the rain. That’s Muni magic.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think a paella is the go-to dish here, but in Gràcia, it's all about the 'pintxos' and a good vermut on a Sunday afternoon.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by their constant fumbling with the T-10 card at the metro turnstile, like it’s a puzzle they haven’t cracked yet.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think 'going to the park' means Clissold. Meanwhile, the locals are all about Abney Park's hidden charms and the graveyard’s peace.
Caught a snippet of a guy on the N68 claiming he knows a secret way to dodge the strikes. Reckoned it’s not all about the trains, just the right folk to ask.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I found a small café with the best türkischer Mokka, and the barista remembers my name. That warm nod feels like family.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Friedrichshain, there’s a spontaneous techno party in a public toilet every summer. Just a guy with a speaker and a whole crowd vibing.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their reaction to a BART delay—it's not frustration, it's a resigned chuckle and a shrug, like, 'What else is new?'

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a three-piece suit playing sax on the bus today, competing with the Bluetooth speaker of someone blasting reggaeton. Classic SF chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think Gràcia's plazas are just for selfies, but locals use them for daily life—catching up, relaxing, or even doing homework.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their puzzled look when asked for directions—especially if they still think the metro is straightforward.
